questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: The gear icon located in the upper right-hand corner of QuickBooks Online provides access to key management areas of the software. It is organized into four named sections for easy navigation. Which of the following correctly lists the four sections found under the QBO gear icon?

answers.text: Your Company, Lists, Tools, and Profile
Company Settings, User Management, Reports, and Tools
Dashboard, Banking, Sales, and Accounting
Account and Settings, Chart of Accounts, Payroll, and Help

explanations.a: The gear icon contains exactly four sections: Your Company, Lists, Tools, and Profile, as described in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: Company Settings and User Management are not the correct section labels; the gear icon uses Your Company, Lists, Tools, and Profile.
explanations.c: Dashboard, Banking, Sales, and Accounting are tabs in the left navigation bar, not sections under the gear icon.
explanations.d: Chart of Accounts is found within the Your Company section of the gear icon, not as a top-level section itself.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: To access QuickBooks Online from any device, users must navigate to the correct web address and enter their credentials. The Student Guide specifies the URL used to reach the QBO login page. Which URL is used to log in to QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: quickbooks.intuit.com/online
qbo.intuit.com
login.quickbooks.com
intuit.com/quickbooks/login

explanations.a: quickbooks.intuit.com/online redirects to marketing pages, not the QBO login screen described in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that users access QuickBooks Online by going to qbo.intuit.com and entering their user ID and password.
explanations.c: login.quickbooks.com is not the URL specified in the Student Guide for accessing the QBO login page.
explanations.d: intuit.com/quickbooks/login is not the URL specified in the Student Guide for the QBO login screen.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: Clicking the +New button at the top of the left navigation bar in QBO reveals a list of transaction screens the user can open. These transaction types are organized into four named groups. Which groups are used to organize the transactions available under +New?

answers.text: Income, Expenses, Payroll, and Banking
Invoices, Bills, Checks, and Deposits
Customers, Vendors, Employees, and Other
Sales, Purchases, Payroll, and Journal Entries

explanations.a: Income, Expenses, Payroll, and Banking are not the grouping labels used in the +New menu.
explanations.b: These are individual transaction types, not the category groupings used to organize the +New menu.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that +New transactions are grouped by Customers, Vendors, Employees, and Other.
explanations.d: Sales, Purchases, Payroll, and Journal Entries are not the group labels used in the +New quick create menu.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: The left navigation bar in QuickBooks Online, located below the +New icon, provides access to all major functional areas of the software. A new QBO user wants to know exactly how many tabs appear in the left navigation bar. How many tabs are in the QBO left navigation bar?

answers.text: Seven
Eight
Nine
Eleven

explanations.a: Seven is too few; the left navigation bar contains eleven tabs in QuickBooks Online.
explanations.b: Eight is incorrect; the Student Guide lists eleven tabs in the left navigation bar.
explanations.c: Nine is incorrect; there are eleven tabs: Dashboard, Banking, Expenses, Sales, Projects, Workers, Reports, Taxes, Mileage, Accounting, and My Accountant.
explanations.d: The left navigation bar contains eleven tabs: Dashboard, Banking, Expenses, Sales, Projects, Workers, Reports, Taxes, Mileage, Accounting, and My Accountant.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A company administrator needs to add a new employee as a QBO user with limited access to sales transactions only. To do this, the administrator must locate the Manage Users feature within QuickBooks Online. Under which section of the gear icon is Manage Users found?

answers.text: Your Company
Lists
Tools
Profile

explanations.a: Manage Users is found under the Your Company section of the gear icon, along with Account and Settings, Custom Form Styles, and Chart of Accounts.
explanations.b: The Lists section of the gear icon contains list management options, not Manage Users.
explanations.c: The Tools section of the gear icon contains items such as Import Data and Reconcile, not Manage Users.
explanations.d: The Profile section of the gear icon contains personal preferences and sign-out options, not Manage Users.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: After logging in to QuickBooks Online, the first screen a user sees is the home screen of the company file. One tab in the left navigation bar is dedicated to returning the user to this starting point at any time during a session. What is the purpose of the Dashboard tab in the QBO left navigation bar?

answers.text: It opens the Banking Center and shows bank feed transactions pending review
It returns the user to the home screen displayed upon first logging in to the QBO company
It displays a running summary of all unpaid invoices and outstanding vendor bills
It opens the Report Center and lists all standard financial reports

explanations.a: The Banking Center is accessed by clicking the Banking tab in the left navigation bar, not the Dashboard.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that clicking Dashboard returns the user to the screen seen when first logging in to a QuickBooks Online company.
explanations.c: Unpaid invoices and outstanding bills are tracked in the Sales and Expenses centers, not the Dashboard tab.
explanations.d: The Report Center is accessed by clicking the Reports tab in the left navigation bar, not the Dashboard.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A business owner wants to add their company logo to all customer-facing forms, change the font color on invoices, and set a default payment method for sales. These customizations are managed in a specific section of Account and Settings. Which Account and Settings section controls the look, feel, and default content of sales forms?

answers.text: Company
Advanced
Sales
Expenses

explanations.a: The Company section stores business information such as company name, address, and EIN, not sales form design.
explanations.b: The Advanced section manages accounting, automation, and time-tracking settings, not the look and feel of sales forms.
explanations.c: The Sales section of Account and Settings controls sales form customization, including templates, logos, colors, fonts, and default content.
explanations.d: The Expenses section manages vendor and purchase settings such as billable expenses and purchase orders, not sales form design.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A QBO Plus subscriber wants to check how close they are to the maximum number of allowed chart of accounts entries and how many of their five company user seats are currently filled. This information is available in a specific section within Account and Settings. What does the Usage section of Account and Settings display?

answers.text: It shows the company's bank account balances compared to the same period last year
It shows all active and inactive users along with their last login timestamps
It shows the total number of transactions entered during the current fiscal year
It shows how much of the subscription's usage limits are currently consumed, such as billable users and chart of accounts entries

explanations.a: Bank account balances are visible in the Banking Center and on the Dashboard, not in the Account and Settings Usage section.
explanations.b: User login history is tracked in the Audit Log, not the Usage section of Account and Settings.
explanations.c: Transaction counts are available through reports such as the Transaction List, not the Usage section.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that the Usage section tells you how much of your subscription's usage limits you are consuming, including billable users, Chart of Accounts, Classes, and Locations.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: An investor in a small business needs to view financial reports from the company's QuickBooks Online file without being able to edit any transactions or see payroll data. The bookkeeper explains that a specific user type was designed exactly for this purpose. Which QBO user type logs into a special version of QBO giving access to almost all reports except payroll and list reports that contain contact information?

answers.text: Reports Only
Standard user with view-only permission selected
Time Tracking Only
Read-Only Admin

explanations.a: The Reports Only user type logs into a special QBO version with access to almost all reports except payroll and list reports with contact info, and is available in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.b: Standard users are not described in the Student Guide as having a view-only mode; Reports Only is the dedicated read-access user type.
explanations.c: Time Tracking Only users access only timesheet entry; they have no access to reports.
explanations.d: Read-Only Admin is not a user type defined in QuickBooks Online; the four types are Standard, Company Admin, Reports Only, and Time Tracking Only.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A construction company wants to give subcontractors limited access to QuickBooks Online so they can fill out their own timesheets without seeing financial data or other users' timesheets. The bookkeeper needs to verify which QBO subscription levels support this restricted user type. In which QBO subscription levels is the Time Tracking Only user type available?

answers.text: All four subscription levels, including Simple Start
Essentials, Plus, and Advanced only
Plus and Advanced only
Advanced only

explanations.a: Simple Start does not support the Time Tracking Only user type; it is only available starting with Essentials.
explanations.b: The Student Guide specifies that Time Tracking Only users are available in QBO Essentials, Plus, and Advanced subscriptions.
explanations.c: Essentials also supports Time Tracking Only users, so Plus and Advanced only is too restrictive.
explanations.d: Advanced only is incorrect; Time Tracking Only is available in Essentials, Plus, and Advanced.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A controller suspects that someone recently changed a vendor's payment information and wants to trace the action back to a specific user and timestamp within QuickBooks Online. The controller knows QBO has a built-in tool to track all user activity and list changes. Which QBO feature is used to monitor logins, third-party activity, and list changes made in the company file?

answers.text: The Banking Center's Reviewed tab, which logs all matched transactions by user
The Scheduled Reports section, which logs when emails were sent and by whom
The Audit Log, accessible from within QuickBooks Online
The Search Transactions advanced filter, filtered by date and user name

explanations.a: The Banking Center's Reviewed tab shows matched bank feed transactions, not a log of user activity or list changes.
explanations.b: Scheduled reports track email delivery of reports, not logins or list changes by user.
explanations.c: The Student Guide lists the Audit Log as the QBO feature used to monitor logins, third-party activity, and list changes.
explanations.d: Advanced Search finds transactions by amount or date but does not log user-level actions or list edits.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A company's accountant wants to prevent anyone from editing transactions dated before December 31 of the prior fiscal year and plans to set a password to protect that historical period. This protection must be configured within Account and Settings. Where in Account and Settings can you close the books and set a closing date password?

answers.text: The Sales section, using the Statements subsection's date restriction tool
The Company section, under the Fiscal Year and tax year fields
The Expenses section, using the bill payment date range control
The Advanced section, which includes an option to enable a closing date with password protection

explanations.a: The Sales section controls sales form design and messaging; it does not include a transaction date lock or closing date feature.
explanations.b: The Company section stores business identity information; fiscal year start month is set there, but closing the books with a password is in Advanced.
explanations.c: The Expenses section manages vendor and purchase settings; it does not include a closing date or password feature.
explanations.d: The Student Guide lists 'Close the books and set a closing date password' as a feature found in the Advanced section of Account and Settings.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A tax preparer asks their client to configure QuickBooks Online so that all reports display using the cash basis of accounting by default rather than accrual. The client needs to locate the correct setting within Account and Settings. In which section of Account and Settings is the default accounting method for reports selected?

answers.text: In Account and Settings, under the Advanced tab in the Accounting subsection
In Account and Settings, under the Sales tab in the Messages subsection
In the Reports Center, under the Customize report toolbar for each report individually
In Account and Settings, under the Company tab in the tax form type field

explanations.a: The Student Guide identifies 'Select your default accounting method for reports (accrual or cash)' as a setting found in the Advanced section of Account and Settings.
explanations.b: The Sales section's Messages subsection controls email content on sales forms, not the default report accounting method.
explanations.c: While individual reports can be switched between cash and accrual, the global default is set in Account and Settings > Advanced, not per-report in the Report Center.
explanations.d: The Company tab stores business identity and tax form type, not the default accounting method for reports.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.objective: 2.4 Custom fields in Sales forms Plus
questions.text: A business using QBO Plus wants to add custom fields to their sales forms to capture additional customer information such as a project code or purchase order reference number. They need to know how many custom fields their subscription allows on sales forms. How many custom fields can be added to sales forms in QBO Plus?

answers.text: Up to five custom fields
Up to three custom fields
Up to ten custom fields
Up to twelve custom fields

explanations.a: Five custom fields is not the correct limit for sales forms in QBO Plus; the Student Guide specifies three.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that QBO subscriptions up to Plus allow up to three custom fields for sales forms.
explanations.c: Ten custom fields is not the limit for QBO Plus sales forms; that figure does not apply to this context.
explanations.d: Twelve custom fields is the limit for QBO Advanced for each of customers, sales, and vendors — not the Plus sales form limit.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A general contractor using QBO Plus wants to start tracking job profitability by associating all transactions, notes, and reports with individual projects. Before the Projects Center becomes accessible from the left navigation bar, a prerequisite step is required. What must be done before the Projects feature is available in QBO Plus?

answers.text: Projects activates automatically the first time a job-related expense transaction is saved
The company must connect at least one bank account before the Projects tab becomes active
Projects must be turned on in Account and Settings under the Advanced tab
A certified ProAdvisor must remotely enable the Projects module on behalf of the company

explanations.a: Projects does not activate automatically from a transaction; it must be manually enabled in Account and Settings.
explanations.b: Connecting a bank account is not a prerequisite for activating the Projects feature; it is enabled through Account and Settings.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that the Projects option must be turned on in Account and Settings under the Advanced tab, and it is only available in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.d: No ProAdvisor involvement is required to enable Projects; any company admin can turn it on in Account and Settings > Advanced.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A business owner is setting up a new Standard user in QuickBooks Online for their office manager and must decide whether to allow the manager to view or edit the company's subscription and billing information. The owner reviews the available options during user setup. How is a Standard user's access to subscription and billing information controlled in QBO?

answers.text: Standard users automatically receive full access to subscription and billing data upon account creation
Standard users can view billing information but are permanently blocked from editing it regardless of settings
Standard users are always blocked from accessing subscription and billing information with no exceptions
The owner chooses during the Standard user's initial setup whether that user can access subscription and billing information

explanations.a: Standard users do not automatically get billing access; the owner explicitly grants or denies this during the setup process.
explanations.b: The Student Guide describes billing access as configurable during setup, not permanently view-only for Standard users.
explanations.c: Standard users can be granted access to subscription and billing information; it is not always blocked.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that when setting up a Standard user, the owner chooses whether that user will have access to subscription and billing information.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A construction firm wants to bill a client in stages as project milestones are completed, creating multiple partial invoices from a single estimate. This workflow requires a feature that must be enabled before it becomes available in the software. Where in QuickBooks Online is Progress Invoicing turned on?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Sales, using the Progress Invoicing toggle
Account and Settings > Advanced, under the Automation settings group
Account and Settings > Expenses, in the purchase order settings area
From the +New menu, by selecting a special Enable Progress Invoicing option

explanations.a: The Student Guide states that Progress Invoicing can be enabled in Account and Settings under the Sales section.
explanations.b: The Advanced section contains automation and project settings, but Progress Invoicing is enabled under Sales, not Advanced.
explanations.c: The Expenses section manages purchase orders and vendor settings; Progress Invoicing is not located there.
explanations.d: Progress Invoicing is not enabled through the +New menu; it requires a setting change in Account and Settings > Sales.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.objective: 2.7 Time Tracking Only in Simple Start
questions.text: A sole proprietor using QBO Simple Start wants to invite a part-time worker as a Time Tracking Only user so the worker can enter their weekly hours without accessing any financial data. The bookkeeper advises the owner on whether this is possible under their current subscription. What happens if a QBO Simple Start subscriber attempts to add a Time Tracking Only user?

answers.text: Time Tracking Only users can be added to Simple Start but are restricted to entering their own hours only with no visibility into others' timesheets
The Time Tracking Only user type is not available in Simple Start; it requires Essentials, Plus, or Advanced
Time Tracking Only users added to Simple Start consume the single company-user seat included in the subscription
Simple Start automatically upgrades to Essentials to accommodate Time Tracking Only users at no additional cost

explanations.a: While Time Tracking Only users do see only their own timesheets, this user type is not available in Simple Start at all.
explanations.b: The Student Guide explicitly states that the Time Tracking Only user type is only available in QBO Essentials, Plus, or Advanced.
explanations.c: Simple Start does not support the Time Tracking Only user type; the option is not available regardless of seat counts.
explanations.d: QuickBooks Online does not automatically upgrade subscriptions; the owner must manually upgrade to access Time Tracking Only users.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: During a Manage Users training session, a bookkeeper asks about the difference between a Company Admin and a Standard user in QuickBooks Online. The trainer explains that the two types have meaningfully different levels of system access. What is the key distinction between a Company Admin and a Standard user in QBO?

answers.text: A Company Admin can only manage payroll and settings, while a Standard user has unrestricted access to all transaction areas
A Standard user has access to all QBO areas except the Chart of Accounts, while a Company Admin has no restrictions
A Company Admin has full access to all areas and subscribed services including payroll, while a Standard user's access to customers, vendors, and admin rights is configured by the owner
A Standard user can add and remove other users but cannot access payroll, while a Company Admin cannot perform user management

explanations.a: This reverses the roles; Company Admins have unrestricted access, while Standard users have configurable, not unlimited, access.
explanations.b: Standard users do not have broad unrestricted access; their permissions for customers, vendors, and admin functions are set by the owner.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that a Company Admin has access to all areas including settings and all subscribed services including payroll, while Standard user access is configured during setup.
explanations.d: Standard users can be granted user management rights by the owner, but they are not the default user management role; that belongs to Company Admins.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A large enterprise company on QBO Advanced wants to add extensive custom data fields to capture information for customers, sales transactions, and vendors far beyond what QBO Plus permits. The team wants to confirm the maximum number of custom fields available in QBO Advanced for each category. How many custom fields does QBO Advanced allow for each of customers, sales, and vendors separately?

answers.text: Up to five custom fields for each of customers, sales, and vendors
Up to eight custom fields for each of customers, sales, and vendors
Up to three custom fields each for customers, sales, and vendors, the same as QBO Plus
Up to twelve custom fields each for customers, sales, and vendors

explanations.a: Five custom fields per category is not the correct limit for QBO Advanced; the Student Guide specifies twelve.
explanations.b: Eight custom fields per category is not the correct Advanced limit; the Student Guide specifies twelve for each of customers, sales, and vendors.
explanations.c: QBO Advanced significantly expands the custom field limit beyond Plus; it allows twelve per category, not the three permitted in Plus.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that QBO Advanced allows up to twelve custom fields each for customers, sales, and vendors.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A regional manager wants to activate both class tracking and location tracking in their QBO Plus file to segment financial data by product line and physical store location. Before transactions can be assigned to classes or locations, this segmentation capability must be switched on. What must be done before class tracking and location tracking are usable in QBO Plus?

answers.text: Both Class tracking and Location tracking must be enabled by toggling them on in Account and Settings > Advanced
Class tracking is enabled in Account and Settings > Sales and Location tracking is enabled separately in Account and Settings > Expenses
At least one class and one location must be created in the Lists area before the tracking feature can be activated
Class and Location tracking activate automatically the first time a transaction is assigned to a department or store

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists 'Turn on Class and/or Location tracking' under the Advanced section of Account and Settings for Plus and Advanced subscriptions.
explanations.b: Both Class and Location tracking are enabled in the same location — Account and Settings > Advanced — not split between Sales and Expenses.
explanations.c: Creating classes or locations is done after the feature is toggled on; creating them is not a prerequisite for activating the setting.
explanations.d: Class and Location tracking do not activate automatically; they must be deliberately enabled in Account and Settings > Advanced.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A company that invoices clients in Canadian dollars and British pounds wants to enable multicurrency support in their QuickBooks Online file so foreign-currency transactions are handled correctly. A new bookkeeper is searching for the correct location in Account and Settings to turn this feature on. In which section of Account and Settings is the Multicurrency option found?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Sales, within the Products and Services subsection
Account and Settings > Advanced, where the Multicurrency option can be toggled on
Account and Settings > Company, under the business name and EIN fields
Account and Settings > Expenses, in the purchase order custom fields area

explanations.a: The Products and Services subsection under Sales controls inventory and pricing settings, not multicurrency.
explanations.b: The Student Guide lists 'Turn on Multicurrency' as a setting found in the Advanced section of Account and Settings.
explanations.c: The Company section stores the business's identity information such as name, address, and EIN, not currency settings.
explanations.d: The Expenses section manages vendor purchase settings and custom fields for purchase orders, not multicurrency support.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A new QBO administrator clicks Add user in the Manage Users screen but nothing opens after the click, leaving the screen unchanged. A support technician remotely reviews the setup and quickly identifies the cause without accessing any QBO settings. Why does the add-user workflow fail when a pop-up blocker is active in the browser?

answers.text: QBO requires pop-ups to display the chart of accounts during the new-user account creation form
Intuit's security system detects the active pop-up blocker and temporarily locks the Manage Users screen as a precaution
Many QBO tasks including adding users are performed in pop-up windows, which the browser blocker prevents from opening
The pop-up blocker intercepts the invitation email delivery process, preventing the system from notifying the new user

explanations.a: The chart of accounts does not appear during user setup; the issue is that the entire add-user dialog opens in a pop-up window.
explanations.b: Intuit does not lock the Manage Users screen in response to pop-up blockers; the window simply fails to open silently.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that QuickBooks Online requires pop-up blockers to be disabled because many tasks, including adding users, are performed in pop-up windows.
explanations.d: The invitation email is sent after the user is configured; the pop-up blocker prevents the setup window from opening in the first place.

questions.name: Navigation & Settings
questions.text: A bookkeeper discovers that the same vendor appears twice in the Vendor List under slightly different names, causing confusion and duplicated data on reports. They follow the merge steps in QBO to consolidate the duplicate into the correct name. After merging two list names in QBO, what happens to the transactions that were assigned to the eliminated name?

answers.text: The eliminated name's transactions are permanently deleted from the system along with the merged entry
The eliminated name's transactions remain linked to the old name as historical read-only records
The eliminated name's transactions are moved to an Unassigned category until the bookkeeper manually reassigns each one
All transactions previously assigned to the eliminated name are automatically reassigned to the surviving merged name

explanations.a: Merging does not delete transactions; the Student Guide states the eliminated name becomes inactive and its transactions are reassigned.
explanations.b: Transactions are not frozen as read-only under the old name; they are actively reassigned to the surviving name upon merge.
explanations.c: There is no Unassigned category in QBO; transactions are automatically moved to the surviving name without manual intervention.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that when two list names are merged, all transactions assigned to the eliminated name are reassigned to the remaining surviving name.
